🎬 Victoria & Abdul (2017)

Victoria & Abdul tells the extraordinary true-inspired story of an unlikely friendship between Queen Victoria, the aging monarch of the British Empire, and Abdul Karim, a young Indian clerk who travels to England to participate in her Golden Jubilee celebrations in 1887. What begins as a brief ceremonial encounter unexpectedly develops into a meaningful relationship when Abdul’s kindness, honesty, and refreshing perspective capture the Queen’s attention. Feeling increasingly isolated by royal responsibilities and surrounded by people who treat her more as a symbol than a person, Victoria finds comfort in Abdul’s companionship and genuine interest in her life. As their friendship grows, Abdul introduces her to Indian culture, language, and traditions, eventually becoming her trusted teacher and personal confidant. However, their unusual bond sparks outrage within the royal household, where members of the court view Abdul’s growing influence with suspicion, jealousy, and prejudice. Determined to protect their friendship, Victoria challenges the expectations of her advisers and family, refusing to allow social conventions to dictate whom she can trust. As tensions escalate, both must navigate cultural differences, political pressures, and the rigid traditions of the British monarchy. Combining heartfelt drama, gentle humor, beautiful historical settings, and emotional storytelling, the film explores friendship, loyalty, cultural understanding, prejudice, loneliness, and the unexpected connections that can change lives.

🎭 Genre: Biography • Drama • History

⭐ IMDb: 6.8/10

⏱️ Runtime: 1h 51m • PG-13

🎥 Director: Stephen Frears

source_details.synopsis: Victoria & Abdul is a 2017 biographical historical drama film directed by Stephen Frears and written by Lee Hall. The film is based on the book Victoria & Abdul: The True Story of the Queen's Closest Confidant by Shrabani Basu, about the real-life relationship between Queen Victoria of the United Kingdom and her Indian Muslim servant Abdul Karim. It stars Judi Dench, Ali Fazal, Michael Gambon, Eddie Izzard, Tim Pigott-Smith (in his final film role), and Adeel Akhtar. The film had its world premiere at the 74th Venice Film Festival and was theatrically released on 15 September 2017 in the United Kingdom. It grossed $68 million worldwide.
